# WebAR Fácil documentation

**[Español](../README.md)** · **English**

WebAR Fácil is an MIT-licensed TypeScript library for building browser-based augmented reality. The standalone build includes the renderer, vision runtime, workers and model decoders. Start with HTML or use the JavaScript API to control the camera, tracking and rendering yourself.

## Start here

1. [Your first HTML app](getting-started.md) gets a JPG or PNG marker and a GLB on screen.
2. [Declarative HTML](declarative.md) describes scene attributes, content and events.
3. [Declarative recipes](recipes.md) adds transforms, animations and transitions.
4. [Installation and distribution](installation.md) explains the standalone, ESM and core builds.

| Goal | Where to start |
| --- | --- |
| Add a model, video, gestures or several image targets | [Declarative HTML](declarative.md), [Interaction](interaction.md), [Multiple markers](multiple-targets.md) |
| Show a model when the camera detects a phone | [Phone recognition](phone-detection.md) |
| Control rendering and the engine in JavaScript | [Programmatic integration](programmatic.md), [WebAREngine](api-engine.md), [Three.js](threejs.md), [A-Frame](aframe.md) |
| Place content in space and recover a saved map | [Spatial tracking](spatial-tracking.md), [Placement](placement.md), [Local maps](maps.md) |
| Tune capture and diagnose tracking | [Camera and performance](camera-performance.md), [Events](events.md), [Diagnostics](diagnostics.md) |
| Check what is implemented and tested | [Generated API](api-generated.md), [Verification](verification.md), [Physical-device acceptance](device-validation.md) |
| Generate a working example with an AI assistant | [AI integration contract](ai-guide.md), [JSON API contract](../api.json) |

## Run an example

The [gallery of 35 examples](../../examples/PRUEBAS/index.html) covers markers, gestures, 3D models, video, surfaces and local maps. Use the [image example](../../examples/declarative.html) for a first test, the [video example](../../examples/declarative-video.html) for chroma key, or the [placement example](../../examples/declarative-placement.html) for a surface.

Image tracking and optical odometry work with ordinary camera capture. Native immersive WebXR depends on the browser and device. Optical placement without a metric reference uses relative scale. [Tracking modes](spatial-tracking.md)

---
Source: docs/en/getting-started.md

# Your first HTML application

## Put three files next to your HTML

```text
my-webar-app/
  index.html
  webar-facil.min.js
  poster.jpg
  model.glb
```

Copy the compiled `webar-facil.min.js` from the distribution. The script contains Three.js, OpenCV/WASM, workers, Draco and Meshopt. Alternatively, point the script tag at a hosted copy of the SDK. Marker and model paths are still relative to your HTML.

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My first WebAR app</title>
  <script defer src="./webar-facil.min.js"></script>
</head>
<body style="margin:0">
  <webar-scene>
    <p role="status">Loading WebAR Fácil…</p>
    <webar-target src="./poster.jpg" target-id="poster" physical-width="0.2">
      <webar-model src="./model.glb" size="0.3" rotation="0 180 0"></webar-model>
    </webar-target>
  </webar-scene>
</body>
</html>
```

## Open the camera and find the marker

1. Serve the directory over localhost on your computer or trusted HTTPS on your phone.
2. Press the scene's camera start button.
3. Print the exact image or show it on another screen and point the camera at it.
4. Stop the scene when finished.

JPG and PNG targets compile on demand. The default marker width is 20 cm. Use the actual printed width in meters when you need scale relative to the marker. A large, sharp and well-lit image is easier to recognize.

## Run the repository

Use Node.js 22.18 or newer and run `npm ci`, then `npm run dev`. Open the [declarative example](../../examples/declarative.html) or the [gallery](../../examples/PRUEBAS/index.html). You only need a static server for a separate project with the compiled SDK.

| Where the HTML lives | Example script path |
| --- | --- |
| Next to the SDK | `./webar-facil.min.js` |
| Repository root | `./dist/webar-facil.min.js` |
| Inside the repository's `examples/` directory | `../dist/webar-facil.min.js` |

`webar-facil.min.js` remains a compatible filename. Both `WebARFacil` and `WebARFacil` expose the same standalone API. If the loading message stays on screen, check the script path and the browser console. [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

---
Source: docs/en/phone-detection.md

# Phone recognition

[Example 31](../../examples/PRUEBAS/31-reconocer-celular.html) uses an optional object detector. Point at another phone and enable «Mostrar detección y confianza» to see the detected box and confidence. Kai follows the box on screen. Inference runs locally in a worker.

## Install the phone detector (example 31)

The detector is optional and distributed separately from `webar-facil.min.js`. To add it to your project, copy `31-reconocer-celular.html`, the entire `phone-detector/` folder alongside the HTML, and the GLB model you want to show.

- Keep `demo.js`, `worker.js`, `tf.min.js`, `coco-ssd.min.js`, `model.json`, and all five files from `group1-shard1of5` through `group1-shard5of5` together. The weights manifest uses those exact names. Include `LICENSE.txt` and keep `README.md` for reference.
- In the HTML, point the first `<script>` to your copy of `webar-facil.min.js` and keep `<script type="module" src="./phone-detector/demo.js"></script>`. If you change the GLB or folder layout, update the path in `demo.js`. The model path resolves relative to `demo.js`, not the HTML.
- Serve the files over HTTPS or use `localhost` during development. The worker loads the weights from its own folder and processes camera frames locally.

Apps that only use markers or SLAM can use the SDK without copying the detector.

---
Source: docs/en/declarative.md

# Applications with declarative HTML

Use `webar-scene` for the camera, renderer and controls. Put each model or video inside its `webar-target` in image mode. In surface mode, put the content directly in the scene. See the [complete first app](getting-started.md).

## Scene attributes

| Attribute | Default or effect |
| --- | --- |
| `mode` | `image`; use `slam` for markerless placement |
| `backend` | `auto` in image mode; `optical-flow` in SLAM mode |
| `slam` | Adds the transition control to an image scene |
| `keep-content-on-lost` | Holds the last displayed transform when enabled |
| `loss-grace` | 500 ms |
| `performance` | `auto`, `balanced`, `battery` or `quality` |
| `camera-width`, `camera-height`, `fps` | Requested capture settings; the browser negotiates the stream |
| `analysis-width`, `analysis-pixels` | Analysis limits; auto/balanced cap at 640 px wide and 307,200 pixels |
| `pixel-ratio`, `antialias` | Renderer controls; default maximum pixel ratio 2 and MSAA enabled |
| `asset-base`, `opencv-url`, `draco-path` | Optional explicit paths for external runtime and decoder assets |
| `gestures`, `min-scale`, `max-scale` | Opt-in selection, rotation and scaling; initial bounds 0.1 and 100 |
| `scan-guide`, `surface-grid` | Marker scan guide and surface grid, enabled by default |
| `placement` | `auto` or `manual`; manual optical placement needs a recent proposal |
| `media-menu`, `fullscreen-view` | Optional capture menu and full-viewport session controls |
| `diagnostics`, `keyframe-correction` | Optional local reports and experimental optical keyframe correction |

Boolean attributes accept an empty value, `true` or `false`. Use CSS to override the default `100dvh` height. Camera/backend configuration is read at startup. Stop, apply the new values and start again when changing those settings. [Camera details](camera-performance.md)

## Image and content attributes

`webar-target` takes a JPG, PNG or compiled WART file through `src`, a `target-id`, and `physical-width` in meters. Omitted IDs become `target-0`, `target-1` and so on. The default physical width is 0.2 m. Use up to eight different images. [Multiple markers](multiple-targets.md)

`webar-model` loads a self-contained GLB, including Draco and Meshopt. Use `size` for the largest dimension (default 0.16), `scale` for uniform or XYZ scaling, `rotation` for XYZ degrees, and `position` for local XYZ coordinates. `animation` accepts an exact name, zero-based index or `none`. By default the first available clip plays.

`webar-video` accepts MP4, `width`, `orientation`, `autoplay`, `muted`, `loop` and chroma options. [Interaction reference](interaction.md)

## Camera and media controls

Use `media-menu` for camera presets, photo and microphone video. Saving and sharing use browser capabilities. The composited recording path applies to web camera scenes. Native immersive WebXR camera imagery is outside that path. Use `fullscreen-view` for full-viewport viewing and a session dialog.

## Use JavaScript with HTML elements

```js
const scene = document.querySelector('webar-scene');
scene.addEventListener('targetFound', event => console.log(event.detail.targetId));
scene.addEventListener('trackingQuality', event => console.log(event.detail.issues));
scene.addEventListener('ar-error', event => console.error(event.detail));
```

| Event | Payload or meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `ar-ready`, `ar-stopped` | Prepared `{app}`, or `null` after stopping |
| `ar-error`, `ar-status` | Error, or `{message}` |
| `ar-pose`, `ar-slam` | Accepted `ARPose`, or transition result |
| `modelLoaded`, `animationFinished` | `{animations}`, or `{name}` |
| `videoLoaded`, `videoPlayBlocked` | `{width,height}`, or playback error |
| `ar-select`, `ar-gesture` | Pointer selection and transforms |
| `contentUpdated`, `ar-placement` | Synchronized content, or placement `{state}` |
| `targetFound`, `targetLost`, `targetVisibility`, `trackingQuality` | Same payloads as the [engine events](events.md) |

`start()`, `stop()`, `refresh()` and `enableSLAM(options?)` return promises. Await `model.updateComplete` after changing a model source. Use `scene.refresh()` after changing the hierarchy. `scene.app` and `scene.engine` are available during the session. Scene `stop()` disposes the managed renderer and resources. Removing the element in an SPA also frees resources.

---
Source: docs/en/interaction.md

# Video, gestures, animation and live content

## Play MP4 and remove a color

```html
<webar-scene gestures>
  <webar-target src="./poster.jpg" target-id="poster">
    <webar-video src="./clip.mp4" width="0.3" orientation="upright"
      autoplay muted loop chroma-key key-color="#00ff00"
      similarity="0.12" smoothness="0.08" spill="0.3"></webar-video>
  </webar-target>
</webar-scene>
```

Use `orientation="flat"` for a plane lying on its anchor and `upright` for a vertical plane. The color, similarity, smoothness and spill controls affect the shader. Try a well-lit, even background. Muted video is more likely to autoplay. When the browser blocks playback, use the scene's play control or start playback from a click. [Video reference](video.md)

## Enable touch gestures

Add `gestures` to the scene or content. Tap a model to select it, drag to rotate it, and pinch to change scale. `min-scale` and `max-scale` bound the multiplier. The gesture transform is local to the content and does not modify the tracked camera pose. Use `ar-select` and `ar-gesture` for custom interaction.

## Choose and control animations

```html
<webar-model src="./avatar.glb" size="0.3" animation="Walk"
  animation-loop="repeat" animation-speed="1.25" animation-fade="0.2"></webar-model>
```

Loop modes are `repeat`, `once` and `pingpong`. `animation-repetitions`, `animation-paused`, and `animation-fade` control repeat count, pause and blending. Listen to `modelLoaded` for clip names and `animationFinished` for completion. The element also exposes `playAnimation(nameOrIndex)` and `stopAnimations()`.

## Replace assets without closing the camera

```js
const model = document.querySelector('webar-model');
model.setAttribute('src', './replacement.glb');
await model.updateComplete;
```

Transforms and playback settings can be updated live. A failed load can be handled with the content error event. When replacing the hierarchy or editing targets, update the DOM and await `scene.refresh()`. Replacing a target can trigger image compilation and change visibility. Changing capture settings or tracking backend follows the session lifecycle.

Try the [live content example](../../examples/declarative-interactive.html), the [video example](../../examples/declarative-video.html), and the [declarative recipes](recipes.md).

---
Source: docs/en/image-targets.md

# Image markers and compilation

## Choose an image

Use a sharp JPG or PNG with distinctive features distributed across the image. A planar print or a static screen works best. Large blank areas, repeating motifs, glare, blur and a very small image in the camera all make matching harder.

```html
<webar-target src="./poster.jpg" target-id="poster" physical-width="0.2">
  <webar-model src="./model.glb"></webar-model>
</webar-target>
```

The scene compiles the target automatically. Use the actual width in meters for physical scale. The tracking transform applies to the image plane and content can be repositioned locally.

## Use the engine compiler

```js
const result = await engine.addImageTarget('poster', './poster.jpg', {
  physicalWidthMeters: 0.2,
  maxDimension: 1024,
});
console.log(result.metadata.quality);
```

The source can be a URL or a Blob/File. The compiler checks input size and format, constrains the working resolution, and extracts features in a worker. The result includes a WART binary buffer and metadata. Quality warnings describe properties such as low texture or weak feature distribution. They are indicators, not a guarantee of real-world detection.

## Compile once and reuse

For a deployment that needs deterministic precompiled assets, use the repository's compiler script or `MarkerCompiler`. Save the binary as `.dat` and load it through `addTarget()` or a declarative target source. The JSON metadata is optional. Keep marker IDs and scale consistent when replacing assets. Use a new URL for a changed image when cache behavior matters.

See the [API reference](api-generated.md) for compiler options, the [quality events](events.md) for live detection, and [multiple markers](multiple-targets.md) for independent targets.

---
Source: docs/en/models.md

# GLB models and animations

## Configure a model

```html
<webar-model src="./model.glb" size="0.3" scale="1"
  position="0 0 0" rotation="0 180 0" animation="Walk"></webar-model>
```

Provide a self-contained GLB. `size` fits its largest dimension and the wrapper positions its base and center. `scale` multiplies that result, with a single factor or XYZ factors. Rotation uses XYZ degrees in HTML. Position is local to the tracked group. Set size relative to your marker or placement backend and inspect it on the target device.

## Load and animate with JavaScript

```js
const model = new WebARFacil.ThreeARModel();
await model.load('./model.glb', { fitSize: 0.3, autoplay: false });
model.playAnimation('Walk', { loop: 'repeat', speed: 1 });
```

Use `fitSize:false` to preserve model units. The renderer should update animation every frame even if no fresh tracking pose arrived. Stop clips when required and dispose the model and scene when leaving a page or route.

## Compression and rendering cost

The standalone includes Draco and Meshopt. For custom builds, configure Draco decoder paths if external assets are used. Compression primarily reduces transfer size. Inspect triangles, texture sizes, materials, draw calls and animation complexity when a scene is slow. Compare the same experience with a lightweight GLB to isolate render cost. [Camera and performance](camera-performance.md)

Change `src` to replace content and await the element's `updateComplete`. Use the [animation example](../../examples/PRUEBAS/15-animaciones-glb.html) to inspect clips and the [interaction guide](interaction.md) for playback controls.

---
Source: docs/en/multiple-targets.md

# Multiple image markers

Use distinct target images and IDs. The same session can track up to eight targets. Different instances of the exact same print are not independent image IDs.

```html
<webar-scene>
  <webar-target src="./poster-a.jpg" target-id="a">
    <webar-model src="./model-a.glb" size="0.3"></webar-model>
  </webar-target>
  <webar-target src="./poster-b.jpg" target-id="b">
    <webar-model src="./model-b.glb" size="0.2"></webar-model>
  </webar-target>
</webar-scene>
```

With JavaScript, bind groups to their IDs or add the models through `app.addContent(id, model)`. Then register targets using `engine.addImageTarget(id, source, options)`. Subscribe to `targetFound`, `targetLost` and `targetVisibility` and route each event using `targetId`. When transitioning from an image to a surface, explicitly choose the target you intend to preserve.

Large images and multiple simultaneous targets can increase matching cost. Check quality per target, choose visually distinct artwork and test at the distance visitors will use. [Multiple-marker example](../../examples/PRUEBAS/14-varios-marcadores.html)

---
Source: docs/en/events.md

# Events, tracking continuity and diagnostics

## Track lifecycle and visibility

| Event | Main fields | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `targetFound` | `targetId`, `timestampMs`, `pose` | First detection or reacquisition |
| `targetLost` | `targetId`, `timestampMs`, `retained`, `reason` | Confirmed loss, removal or stop |
| `targetVisibility` | `targetId`, `visible`, `reason` | Control visibility in a custom renderer |
| `trackingQuality` | `targetId`, `timestampMs`, `state`, `score`, `processingMs`, `issues`, `diagnosis` | Guide users and diagnose tracking |

Listen through `scene.addEventListener(name, callback)` and read `event.detail`, or subscribe via `engine.on(name, callback)`. The engine returns an unsubscribe function. `ar-ready` means the scene is prepared. Use target events to determine whether a marker is visible.

## Avoid flicker and restarts

The loss grace period absorbs brief interruptions. The target states are `tracking`, `recovering` and `lost`. Found/lost events occur on transitions, so load assets once and keep playback independent of these events. Enable `keep-content-on-lost` to retain the last displayed transform after confirmed loss. In a running scene, call `scene.engine.setKeepContentOnLost(enabled)` and update the attribute for the next session.

```js
const scene = document.querySelector('webar-scene');
scene.addEventListener('trackingQuality', ({detail}) => {
  if (detail.issues.includes('small-target')) console.log('Move closer');
  if (detail.issues.includes('blur')) console.log('Hold the camera steady');
});
```

Quality scores range from 0 to 1 and are heuristic. Use motion, inlier count and measured timings with the issue labels. [Diagnostics](diagnostics.md)

---
Source: docs/en/recipes.md

# Declarative HTML recipes

## Size, rotation and animation

```html
<webar-model id="avatar" src="./avatar.glb" size="0.3"
  rotation="0 180 0" animation="Walk" animation-loop="repeat"></webar-model>
```

```js
const avatar = document.querySelector('#avatar');
avatar.setAttribute('size', '0.45');
avatar.setAttribute('rotation', '0 90 0');
avatar.addEventListener('modelLoaded', ({detail}) => console.log(detail.animations));
```

To retain content after the marker disappears, enable `keep-content-on-lost` on the scene. During a running session use the engine method and keep the markup in sync if the choice should survive restart. A retained object stays on the last known transform.

## Change a model from a button

```js
document.querySelector('#change-model').onclick = async () => {
  const avatar = document.querySelector('#avatar');
  avatar.setAttribute('src', './second.glb');
  await avatar.updateComplete;
};
```

Use a different target ID when the physical image changes. Use `scene.refresh()` after DOM hierarchy changes. When you only update a model source, retain the original target and camera.

## Place content on a surface

```html
<webar-scene mode="slam" backend="optical-flow" placement="manual">
  <webar-model src="./model.glb" size="0.5"></webar-model>
</webar-scene>
```

To transition from image mode, add `slam` to the scene. Start on the marker, then use the transition control. Confirm the proposed location if the chosen placement mode requires confirmation. [Spatial transitions](spatial-tracking.md)

For hands-on examples, see the [gallery](../../examples/PRUEBAS/index.html) and the [advanced recipes](recipes-programmatic.md).

---
Source: docs/en/spatial-tracking.md

# Spatial tracking with WebXR and optical fallback

WebXR and optical tracking both expose placement poses. Select the backend with `backend="auto"`, `backend="webxr"`, or `backend="optical-flow"`. Auto can use WebXR when immersive AR and hit testing are available. Use the optical backend to test camera-based tracking explicitly, including on iOS browsers where immersive AR is unavailable. A declarative SLAM scene defaults to optical tracking.

```html
<webar-scene mode="slam" backend="optical-flow" placement="manual">
  <webar-model src="./chair.glb" size="0.5"></webar-model>
</webar-scene>
```

1. Open the page over HTTPS and start AR with the scene button.
2. Aim at a textured surface and move the phone slowly to produce parallax.
3. Wait for a placement guide and confirm the position.
4. Move sideways and return to the initial view to inspect drift.

In native WebXR, accept the browser’s immersive prompt and confirm placement inside the session. Optical tracking estimates camera motion and a local surface from frames. Its scale is relative when no metric reference is available. A marker with a known physical width can seed metric scale under suitable conditions. Markerless metric tracking remains experimental. Use [device validation](device-validation.md) to compare backends.

---
Source: docs/en/placement.md

# Visual guidance and placement confirmation

After placing content in example 30, walk normally. The map automatically collects viewpoints along the route. If tracking is lost, the example attempts to recover the original placement. «Otra zona» starts a new map.

In [example 30](../../examples/PRUEBAS/30-explorar-superficies.html), tap to choose an area of the optical SLAM plane to inspect. Blue dots highlight contrast in the camera feed and yellow dots show map points near the plane. The green area marks the extent supported by those points. Tap the area or select «Usar zona» to preview a GLB or MP4. Pinch to resize the grid within the detected area or to scale the content.

The image scan guide tells users where to aim. The surface guide previews where spatial content will be placed. With `placement="manual"` the user confirms before the model becomes anchored.

| State | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Scanning for image | Put the whole marker in view and avoid glare. |
| Searching for a surface | Aim at a textured area and move sideways gently. |
| Surface proposed | Inspect the grid and confirm placement. |
| Content anchored | Walk around the model and verify that it stays near the selected point. |

The optical grid reflects a local estimate. If it straddles a tabletop and an object, move the view until the intended area fills the center and reacquire a proposal. Use the [spatial tracking chapter](spatial-tracking.md) to choose the backend.

## Matches and recovery in example 30

Optical SLAM compares each recovery frame against up to **50 saved views**. It evaluates each view separately. A visual match pairs similar ORB descriptors. A geometrically consistent point (*inlier*) is a match that also fits the estimated camera position and orientation.

| Message in the example | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| No matches found | None of the saved views produced any matches. |
| Few matches found | The best view produced 1 to 14 matches. The engine needs 15 before attempting pose estimation. |
| Matches found, but insufficient to confirm | At least one view produced 15 or more matches, but none passed geometric validation. |
| Candidate pose found | The estimate passed basic validation and needs a second compatible observation. |

**Basic validation** requires at least 15 geometrically consistent points, at least 40% of that view's matches, and coverage across at least 4 image cells. The bounding rectangle of those points must cover at least 8% of the analyzed frame.

**Single-frame confirmation** requires at least 30 inliers, a 65% inlier ratio, coverage across 6 cells, and reprojection error below 1.5 pixels. If the estimate only passes basic validation, the engine requires two compatible observations. If a tabletop has little texture, frame its edges and surroundings to give the engine more visual references.
## Environment mesh (example 32)

The [mesh and occlusion example](../../examples/PRUEBAS/32-malla-entorno.html) uses optical tracking with an RGB camera. Move the phone sideways over a textured surface, tap a triangle to place Kai, then change your viewpoint. “Mostrar malla” shows the geometry and “Oclusión” enables depth writes so the geometry can hide parts of the model.

The scene uses `ThreeARScene` and calls `exportSLAMMap()` at most once every 500 ms, after the previous export has completed. It triangulates only new keyframes by projecting their points onto a grid and connecting neighbors at similar depths. Triangles accumulate in floor-aligned 3D blocks, with duplicate triangles filtered by quantized vertex positions. Blocks remain in memory for the session after keyframes are replaced. A raycast places Kai and scanning continues until you pause it.

The coverage panel shows a top view of blocks with triangles and the current camera position. Individual blocks can contain gaps. The demo budgets 96 blocks and 256 triangles per block, for a theoretical maximum of 24,576. Other blocks can still grow when a block is full. Block size comes from the first camera-to-surface distance and uses relative map units.

The reconstruction is experimental, partial, and relative in scale. Smooth walls can have gaps, and edges, glass, and moving objects can produce poor estimates. Tracking loss hides the mesh and model. If the map resets, scan again and place the model again.

After pointing the camera away and returning, compare the mesh with an identifiable physical edge. A shift while tracking stays active may come from pose drift or errors in the estimated geometry. The demo enables local keyframe correction and reports when the engine adjusts or relocalizes the camera. It corrects the pose when enough verified matches are available. Stored blocks keep their geometry, and the counter measures coverage rather than accuracy.
## Object point cloud (example 33)

In [example 33](../../examples/PRUEBAS/33-mapa-3d-objeto.html), keep a textured object still and capture up to 24 views from different positions. Move around it while keeping shared details in frame. Use the lower viewer to rotate and zoom the cloud. Each color shows which view first contributed those points. After each capture, the app reports how many new points were added.

The scene requests the current keyframe via `exportSLAMMap({includeCurrentView:true})`, selects landmarks within the framing guide, and keeps the 3D cluster connected to the center. Each additional view must share points with the accumulated cloud. It accumulates landmarks in map coordinates and merges duplicates by 3D cell. The cloud is sparse, uses relative scale, and may include the background. It remains in memory while the page is open. This demo does not yet use the cloud to recognize the object in a new session.
## Cylindrical label (example 34)

[Example 34](../../examples/PRUEBAS/34-etiqueta-curva.html) accepts an unwrapped JPG or PNG label and includes a printable 100 mm sample. Measure the outer diameter across the straight section and the label width along the curve, using the visible width if the paper overlaps. Label height follows the image aspect ratio.

Call `engine.addImageTarget('label', image, {physicalWidthMeters: 0.1, cylinderDiameterMeters: 0.066})`. The anchor sits on the cylinder axis at the label's mid-height. Curvature is applied at registration and WART retains the flat image descriptors. Tracking is experimental and requires a textured label on a constant-diameter section. Conical bottles and transfer from a curved-label pose to a SLAM anchor are outside this example.
## Hand interaction (example 35)

In [example 35](../../examples/PRUEBAS/35-interaccion-manos.html), MediaPipe Hand Landmarker tracks the index fingertip on the same video stream as AR. Add `<webar-hands cursor gesture="pinch"></webar-hands>` to the scene and mark selectable models with `hand-target`. Aim at a model and bring your index finger and thumb together. The model emits `ar-hand-tap` with `detail.element`, `detail.object`, `detail.point` (the 3D hit position) and `detail.gesture`. With `gesture="dwell"`, holding the cursor over the same model for 650 ms triggers an interaction.

The fingertip is projected onto the 3D scene from its camera image coordinates. This supports mid-air pointing and does not measure physical distance between the finger and the virtual object. The component uses the video of a declarative Three.js scene and suspends detection during immersive WebXR.

Use `runtime-src`, `wasm-path`, and `model-src` to self-host the ESM module, its WASM directory, and `hand_landmarker.task`. By default they load when a scene with hand interaction starts. Camera frames are processed in the browser. Listen for `hand-ready` and `hand-error` to report status. Synchronous inference uses reduced-resolution video and an `fps` limit (12 by default, range 1 to 20). On `webar-scene`, `facing-mode="user"` requests the front camera and `facing-mode="environment"` requests the rear camera.

---
Source: docs/en/diagnostics.md

# Local diagnostics for iPhone and Android

Use diagnostics in development to reproduce camera, rendering and tracking problems. For a controlled comparison, use the same marker or surface, camera distance, scene and sequence of movements on both phones. Record the browser, backend and performance preset with each run.

1. Open the development diagnostics tool over HTTPS.
2. Start one scene and let the camera settle before collecting a baseline.
3. Repeat the action that causes the issue, such as covering the marker or moving the phone sideways.
4. Export the report and identify the run by device and scenario.

| Observation | Signals to compare |
| --- | --- |
| Model stutters while marker stays visible | Render cadence, frame time, model complexity and device load. |
| Model jumps after occlusion | Target loss and recovery events, pose quality and marker size in frame. |
| Optical anchor moves with camera motion | Backend, initialization, parallax and relocalization. |

Development diagnostics use structured measurements. The public gallery omits the report controls. See [camera and performance](camera-performance.md) and [odometry validation](odometry-validation.md).

---
Source: docs/en/odometry-validation.md

# Validating odometry, relocalization and drift

Treat acquisition, tracking and recovery as separate measurements. Repeat each test several times on the same textured surface, with the same route and lighting, and record conditions such as glare and autofocus hunting.

| Test | Procedure | Record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Initialization | Move laterally until a surface can be selected. | Time to first valid placement. |
| Drift | Place an object, walk a short loop and return to the starting view. | Offset from the original placement and tracking interruptions. |
| Recovery | Briefly cover the camera or look away, then return to the mapped view. | Whether the pose recovers and how long recovery takes. |
| Reload | Save and restore an optical map, then revisit the original viewpoint. | Whether the environment relocalizes and the anchor returns. |

For optical sessions initialized without metric scale, compare alignment visually or in relative units. For measurements in meters, use a known-size reference and check the result against a physical measurement. Compare like-for-like backends and keep failed runs in the record. See [local maps](maps.md) and [physical-device acceptance](device-validation.md).

---
Source: docs/en/installation.md

# Installation and distribution

The hosted standalone script registers custom elements and includes Three.js. Place it in the page head with `defer`, then declare the scene in the body.

The npm package is named `webar-facil`. Use `WebARFacil` in new classic-script integrations. Classic builds also expose the legacy `MiLibreriaAR` alias for existing integrations.

```html
<script defer src="https://realidad-aumentada.com.co/webar-facil/webar-facil.min.js"></script>
```

Choose the distribution based on how the application is built.

| Application | Use |
| --- | --- |
| Plain HTML | Hosted standalone script and declarative elements. |
| Existing JavaScript application | The standalone global or the package exports in a bundler. |
| Source checkout or GitHub ZIP | Run `npm ci` and `npm run build`, then inspect `dist/`. |

A model, marker or video URL in your HTML resolves against your page. Put assets beside your page or use absolute URLs served with compatible CORS headers. Use HTTPS for device testing. See [local release](local-release.md) and [deployment](deployment.md).

---
Source: docs/en/local-release.md

# Identifying and serving a local build

From a source checkout, build the distributable and serve it through HTTP on localhost or HTTPS on another device.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
npm run docs:check
npm run dev
```

The build creates `dist/webar-facil.min.js`, the documentation and the example gallery. Use the local server URL printed by the development command and follow the example’s paths. To verify what a browser loaded, inspect the SDK script in the Network panel and use the exported `LIBRARY_VERSION` and `LIBRARY_BUILD` from the loaded SDK when troubleshooting a stale copy.

The hosted script URL is documented in [installation](installation.md). For a portable release, review [release preparation](alpha-release.md) and [implementation verification](verification.md).

---
Source: docs/en/alpha-release.md

# Preparing the public alpha

Before distributing a GitHub archive or updating the hosted bundle, verify it from a clean extraction. Include the MIT license, dependency notices, source, lockfile, documentation and runnable examples. Keep development reports, environment settings and installed dependencies out of the archive.

- Build and run the documentation checks from the extracted copy.
- Start with the declarative marker example, then test video and spatial placement.
- Check that the English and Spanish manuals contain the same chapters and link to each other.
- Record results separately for desktop, iOS and Android. Record backend and browser for spatial tests.
- Keep experimental markerless metric placement visibly identified in its example.

See [contributing](contributing.md) for commands and [device validation](device-validation.md) for acceptance scenarios.

Source: docs/en/camera-performance.md

# Camera, focus and performance

Set `performance` on the scene. The preset influences capture and processing budgets. Actual video dimensions, frame rate and focus capabilities depend on the camera track and browser.

```html
<webar-scene performance="auto">
  <webar-target src="./poster.jpg" target-id="poster">
    <webar-model src="./model.glb" size="0.35"></webar-model>
  </webar-target>
</webar-scene>
```

| Profile | Typical use |
| --- | --- |
| `auto` | Start here when the device capabilities are unknown. |
| `battery` | Reduce processing load for long sessions or constrained hardware. |
| `balanced` | Compare tracking and render cadence under a consistent workload. |
| `quality` | Test whether additional detail helps a small or distant marker. |

Compare a lightweight model and the production GLB with the same marker and profile. If tracking remains steady while rendering slows, inspect geometry, texture sizes and draw calls. If detection worsens as resolution falls, let the marker occupy more of the image. Test camera switching and autofocus on the physical device before drawing conclusions from a desktop webcam. See [diagnostics](diagnostics.md).

---
Source: docs/en/deployment.md

# Deployment and browser security

Serve production pages and device previews over HTTPS. Desktop loopback URLs can use a secure-context exception. For a phone on your LAN, use an HTTPS host that the phone trusts. Open the page from its served URL so that scripts, models, images and media resolve over HTTP or HTTPS.

| Resource | Deployment check |
| --- | --- |
| SDK | Script returns JavaScript and loads before AR initialization. |
| Marker and model | URLs resolve relative to the document, with exact filename casing. |
| Video | Browser can decode the container and codec. Cross-origin hosting permits access when used as a texture. |
| Camera or microphone | Permission granted by the browser and any enclosing iframe policy. |

If the page is embedded, the host page must allow the required features through its permissions policy and iframe configuration. Open the page directly to isolate iframe restrictions. Use the [troubleshooting guide](troubleshooting.md) to separate network and camera failures.

---
Source: docs/en/troubleshooting.md

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page shows “Loading SDK” | Network panel, SDK response and console. | Correct the script URL and confirm the response contains JavaScript. |
| Camera button does nothing | Secure context, browser permissions and other apps using the camera. | Open the HTTPS page directly and retry from a fresh tab. |
| Module fetch fails | Exact URL, response status and content type. | Serve the current standalone build or copy the runtime files required by an older build. |
| Model never appears | Marker detected event, model URL and size. | Verify the original marker, then test the GLB in the simplest example. |
| Video appears black | Codec support, autoplay policy and CORS. | Use a supported MP4 and start it from a user interaction if required. |
| SLAM guide appears but content does not | Placement confirmation. | Use the scene’s placement button or select within native WebXR. |
| Content jumps or drifts | Backend, texture, motion and scale. | Test a textured area and follow the [odometry procedure](odometry-validation.md). |

For reproducible reports, include the browser, device, exact page, backend and steps to trigger the issue. Capture the first console error and check its URL before chasing subsequent failures.

---
Source: docs/en/concepts.md

# Concepts and coordinate systems

| Term | Meaning in WebAR Fácil |
| --- | --- |
| Target | Reference image and its precomputed features. |
| Model-view matrix | Target or anchor transform expressed in camera coordinates. |
| Projection matrix | Camera intrinsics expressed for the renderer, including the near and far planes. |
| Anchor | A content transform retained relative to a spatial reference. |
| Content transform | The model's local position, scale and rotation relative to the tracked parent. |

Pose matrices have 16 elements in column-major order. Treat the projection and model-view as a pair and let the wrapper apply the conventions it expects. With a custom renderer, align the projected viewport with the displayed video crop. Apply visual offsets to a child of the tracked group so a new pose can update the parent independently. The optical backend uses relative units until initialized with a metric reference.

---
Source: docs/en/programmatic.md

# Advanced programmatic integration

Use `ThreeARScene` when the application needs buttons, application state or runtime content changes while delegating rendering and camera composition to the library. The scene owns a renderer, camera, lights and animation loop. Load your assets, start the camera from a user action and register the image target.

```js
const { ThreeARScene, ThreeARModel } = window.WebARFacil;
const app = new ThreeARScene({ container: document.querySelector('#view') });
const model = new ThreeARModel();
app.addContent('poster', model);
document.querySelector('#start').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  try {
    await app.engine.startCamera();
    await app.engine.addImageTarget('poster', './poster.jpg', { physicalWidthMeters: 0.2 });
    await model.load('./robot.glb');
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(error);
    await app.engine.stop();
  }
});
```

Match the target ID used by `addContent` and `addImageTarget`. Call `app.dispose()` on unmount. If you stop and restart the engine, register your targets again. For the declarative equivalent see [first application](getting-started.md). For an existing renderer see [Three.js](threejs.md).

---
Source: docs/en/recipes-programmatic.md

# Advanced programmatic recipes

## Use files picked by the user

Pass an image File to `addImageTarget`. For a GLB, create an object URL and release it when loading has finished. Load a replacement on the existing model so it stays associated with the target ID.

```js
await app.engine.addImageTarget('poster', imageInput.files[0], { physicalWidthMeters: 0.2 });
const url = URL.createObjectURL(modelInput.files[0]);
try {
  await model.load(url);
} finally {
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}
```

In production, check that the inputs contain files and surface load failures near the corresponding control. Use a single controller to serialize start, stop and content changes.

## Export descriptors or preserve a local map

The [marker chapter](image-targets.md) describes how to export precomputed targets. When using optical SLAM, persist the structured snapshot described in [local maps](maps.md). Store typed arrays using IndexedDB's structured clone support.

## Unmount an experience

Remove listeners created by your page, revoke object URLs you still own, then await `app.dispose()` so the camera, renderer and owned content are released. When mounting another route, create a fresh scene.


## Editable text in AR

Draw the text on a canvas and use it as a `THREE.CanvasTexture` on a `THREE.Sprite`. Redraw on input and set `needsUpdate = true`. Add the sprite to the image or spatial anchor after `ar-ready`.

[Example 4](../../examples/PRUEBAS/04-texto-marcador.html) · [Example 10](../../examples/PRUEBAS/10-texto-slam.html)

## Control scene lighting

On `ar-ready`, get the Three.js scene from `scene.app.scene`. Find the directional light and use the slider value to update its position. Apply the initial value when the scene is ready and update it on `input`.

[Example 6](../../examples/PRUEBAS/06-iluminacion-marcador.html) · [Example 12](../../examples/PRUEBAS/12-iluminacion-slam.html)

## Select model parts

Convert the pointer position to normalized canvas coordinates and use `THREE.Raycaster` with the scene camera. Highlight the first intersected mesh and save its original material state so you can clear the selection.

[Example 19](../../examples/PRUEBAS/19-seleccionar-partes.html)

## Change catalog colors

Update the model's `src` and await `updateComplete`. Then traverse the GLB, find the meshes you want to tint and call `material.color.set(...)`. Reapply the tint when the color input changes.

[Example 20](../../examples/PRUEBAS/20-catalogo-colores.html)

## Combine model text and video

Put the GLB and MP4 in the same `webar-target`. Add the text sprite to the same anchor. Each item has its own visibility or playback control.

[Example 24](../../examples/PRUEBAS/24-contenido-compuesto.html)

---
Source: docs/en/video.md

# MP4 video and chroma key

```html
<webar-target src="./poster.jpg" target-id="poster">
  <webar-video src="./clip.mp4" width="0.3" orientation="upright"
    chroma-key muted loop></webar-video>
</webar-target>
```

Set `orientation="upright"` to stand the video up or `orientation="flat"` to lay it along the marker. Use `chroma-key` for a uniform key background and tune `key-color`, `similarity`, `smoothness` and `spill` using the actual footage. A compatible MP4 with a flat, evenly lit background produces a cleaner cutout. Muted playback works with more autoplay policies. For audio, provide a user action that starts playback and handle browser rejection.

In a custom Three.js scene, `ThreeARVideo` provides the equivalent programmatic content. Manage its playback and disposal with the scene lifecycle. If a remote video plays as a plain HTML element but fails as a texture, check its CORS response headers.

---
Source: docs/en/threejs.md

# Three.js integration

Use the standalone bundle's `THREE` namespace together with its wrappers, or import the module build and Three.js through the same bundler setup. Keep objects and loaders on a compatible Three.js instance.

| Wrapper | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `ThreeARScene` | Managed camera, renderer, render loop and pose application. |
| `ThreeARGroup` | Tracked transform for an existing scene graph. |
| `ThreeARModel` | GLB loading, model normalization and animation. |
| `ThreeARVideo` | Video texture and optional chroma material. |

## Use an existing renderer

[Example 29 · Three.js with a custom renderer](../../examples/PRUEBAS/29-threejs.html) shows an animated GLB on an image target with the camera, projection and render loop managed in JavaScript.

Bind the tracked group to the target ID. The group applies the world matrix and follows engine visibility. Derive the camera transform from the inverse view matrix and apply the matching projection.

```js
const tracked = new ThreeARGroup().bind(engine, 'poster');
scene.add(tracked);
camera.matrixAutoUpdate = false;
const unsubscribe = engine.onPose((_matrix, pose) => {
  if (pose.backend === 'webxr') return;
  camera.matrix.fromArray(pose.viewMatrix).invert();
  camera.updateMatrixWorld(true);
  if (pose.projectionMatrix) {
    camera.projectionMatrix.fromArray(pose.projectionMatrix);
    camera.projectionMatrixInverse.copy(camera.projectionMatrix).invert();
  }
});
```

Use a child for local transforms. Keep the viewport and video crop aligned. If you only have model-view and update the group manually, use an identity camera. In immersive WebXR the renderer owns the XR camera and frame loop. On teardown, call `unsubscribe()` and `tracked.dispose()`, then release your own scene objects. See [the complete custom app](../../examples/custom-app.html) and [coordinates](concepts.md).

---
Source: docs/en/aframe.md

# A-Frame integration

Load A-Frame first, create an engine and register the official components before A-Frame initializes the associated scene. The tracker component binds the entity to a target ID, while model and video components provide content helpers.

```js
const { WebAREngine, registerAFrameComponent, registerAFrameModelComponent,
  registerAFrameVideoComponent } = window.WebARFacil;
const engine = new WebAREngine();
registerAFrameComponent(AFRAME, engine);
registerAFrameModelComponent(AFRAME);
registerAFrameVideoComponent(AFRAME);
```

```html
<a-entity my-ar-tracker="targetId: poster">
  <a-entity gltf-model="url(./robot.glb)" scale="0.2 0.2 0.2"></a-entity>
</a-entity>
```

Start the engine from a button and register the same `poster` ID. Put authored transforms on a child entity, because tracking controls the parent's matrix. If another A-Frame component also drives the camera, resolve that ownership before starting AR. See [engine API](api-engine.md).

| Component | Properties |
| --- | --- |
| `my-ar-tracker` | `target`, `targetId`, `physicalWidth` |
| `my-ar-model` | `src`, `fitSize`, `autoplay` |
| `my-ar-video` | `src`, `width`, `chromaKey`, `keyColor`, `similarity`, `smoothness`, `spill`, `muted`, `loop` |

Set the tracker component's `target` after the camera starts if you want it to load the reference. A `.dat` file goes through compiled target loading. An image URL is compiled by the engine. Listen for `ar-error` on the tracker and `ar-model-error` on the model. If you remove the entity that owns a marker, remove its target explicitly with `engine.removeTarget(id)`. See the [complete A-Frame example](../../examples/PRUEBAS/25-aframe.html).

---
Source: docs/en/maps.md

# Persisting local optical maps

An optical map stores a bounded set of local keyframes used for relocalization. The engine keeps it in memory during the session. Applications may save it explicitly and restore it into a later optical session. Use the same physical space and revisit a mapped viewpoint under similar lighting.

```js
const snapshot = await engine.exportSLAMMap();
// Store snapshot with IndexedDB's structured clone support.
const restored = await readSavedMap();
await engine.importSLAMMap(restored);
```

The snapshot carries a schema version, an optical map, a target ID and an optional anchor transform. The map includes camera intrinsics, a scale, a map ID and keyframes with descriptors, points and view matrices. Preserve typed arrays and reject incompatible or corrupt snapshots. Snapshots contain scene geometry and descriptors. Keep them private by default and give users a way to delete them from application storage.

Use compatible camera, lens, capture dimensions and projection on restore. An imported anchor is eligible for display after the camera relocalizes against the environment. Native WebXR maps are managed by the platform and are outside this API. Unseeded optical maps use relative scale and may drift. See the [IndexedDB map example](../../examples/PRUEBAS/13-mapas-locales.html) and [odometry tests](odometry-validation.md).

---
Source: docs/en/api-engine.md

# WebAREngine

`WebAREngine` manages camera access, image tracking, spatial tracking and event subscriptions. Create a scene wrapper for a managed renderer, or supply your own renderer and consume the engine's poses.

| Task | Public method |
| --- | --- |
| Start camera | `startCamera()` |
| Register an image | `addImageTarget(id, source, options)` |
| Load a compiled target | `loadTarget(url)` |
| Start spatial tracking | `enableSLAM(options)` |
| Listen for transforms | `onPose(callback)` |
| Listen for visibility or quality | `on('targetFound', callback)`, `on('targetLost', callback)`, `on('trackingQuality', callback)` |
| Persist an optical map | `exportSLAMMap()`, `importSLAMMap(snapshot)` |
| Release the session | `stop()` |

Pass a measured `physicalWidthMeters` when size matters. Set `imageLossGraceMs` and `keepContentOnLost` to control temporary loss and final visibility. Await operations that change tracking state and dispose of application listeners on unmount. See the [generated reference](api-generated.md) for exact types.

---
Source: docs/en/api-generated.md

```ts
import { type CameraManagerOptions, type CameraMetrics } from './camera/CameraManager.js';
import { type TrackerOptions } from './tracking/Tracker.js';
import { type MarkerQuality } from './tracking/ImageCompiler.js';
import { type OpticalFlowOptions } from './slam/OpticalFlowSLAM.js';

import type { ARPose, CameraIntrinsics } from './Pose.js';

import type { AREventMap } from './tracking/events.js';
export declare enum EngineState {
    Idle = "Idle",
    Camera = "Camera",
    TrackingImage = "TrackingImage",
    TrackingSurface = "TrackingSurface",
    Disposed = "Disposed"
}
export interface EngineOptions {
    experimentalMetricScale?: ExperimentalMetricScale;
    keyframeCorrection?: boolean;
    imageLossGraceMs?: number;
    keepContentOnLost?: boolean;
    imageSmoothingMs?: number;
    camera?: Omit<CameraManagerOptions, 'onFrame' | 'onError'>;

}

}

    targetId: string;
}

    constructor(options?: EngineOptions);
    get state(): EngineState;

    get cameraSettings(): MediaTrackSettings | null;
    get calibration(): CameraIntrinsics | undefined;

    onStatus(fn: (message: string) => void): () => void;
    onError(fn: (error: Error) => void): () => void;
    onSurface(fn: (matrix: Float32Array) => void): () => void;
    onMetrics(fn: (metrics: CameraMetrics) => void): () => void;
    get targetIds(): readonly string[];
    on<K extends keyof AREventMap>(name: K, listener: (event: AREventMap[K]) => void): () => void;
    onTargetFound(listener: (event: AREventMap['targetFound']) => void): () => void;
    onTargetLost(listener: (event: AREventMap['targetLost']) => void): () => void;
    onTrackingQuality(listener: (event: AREventMap['trackingQuality']) => void): () => void;
    onTargetVisibility(listener: (event: AREventMap['targetVisibility']) => void): () => void;
    setKeepContentOnLost(value: boolean, targetId?: string): void;
    checkSLAMVisualReference(action: 'capture' | 'verify', id: string): Promise<VisualReferenceResult>;

        includeCurrentView?: boolean;
    }): Promise<SLAMMapSnapshot>;
    importSLAMMap(snapshot: SLAMMapSnapshot): Promise<void>;
    startCamera(): Promise<void>;
    loadTarget(url: string | URL): Promise<void>;
    addTarget(id: string, url: string | URL): Promise<void>;
    loadImageTarget(source: Blob | string | URL, options?: ImageTargetOptions): Promise<ImageTargetResult>;

    removeTarget(id: string): Promise<void>;
    enableSLAM(options?: SurfaceTransitionOptions): Promise<SurfaceTransitionResult>;
    stop(): Promise<void>;
    dispose(): void;
}
```

## diagnostics/ARDiagnostics.d.ts

```ts
import { TRACKING_STAGES, TRACKING_COUNTS } from '../tracking/profile.js';
import type { WebAREngine } from '../WebAREngine.js';
import type { CameraMetrics } from '../camera/CameraManager.js';
import { ODOMETRY_STAGES } from '../slam/OdometryBackend.js';
export type DeviceTestResult = 'pending' | 'pass' | 'fail' | 'not-supported';
export interface DiagnosticContext {
    platform?: 'ios' | 'android' | 'desktop' | 'other';
    execution?: 'unspecified' | 'automated' | 'physical-user-reported';
    deviceModel?: string;
    osVersion?: string;
    browserVersion?: string;
    scenario?: string;
}
export interface DiagnosticConfiguration {
    mode?: string;
    backend?: string;
    performance?: string;
    maxFramePixels?: number;
    analysisWidth?: number;
    requestedFPS?: number;
    lossGraceMs?: number;
    keepContentOnLost?: boolean;
    manualPlacement?: boolean;
    keyframeCorrection?: boolean;
    renderPixelRatio?: number;
    antialias?: boolean;
}
export interface DiagnosticOptions {
    context?: DiagnosticContext;
    configuration?: DiagnosticConfiguration;
    sampleLimit?: number;
    now?: () => number;
}
export interface DiagnosticStats {
    count: number;
    mean: number | null;
    min: number | null;
    max: number | null;
    p50: number | null;
    p95: number | null;
    quantileSamples: number;
}
export interface DiagnosticRendererMetrics {
    drawCalls: number;
    triangles: number;
    geometries: number;
    textures: number;
    drawingBufferWidth: number;
    drawingBufferHeight: number;
    pixelRatio: number;
}
export interface DiagnosticReport {
    schemaVersion: 1;
    kind: 'webar-diagnostics';
    sdk: {
        version: string;
        build: string;
    };
    createdAt: string;
    durationMs: number;
    recording: boolean;
    context: Required<DiagnosticContext>;
    configuration: DiagnosticConfiguration;
    environment: {
        userAgent: string;
        secureContext: boolean;
        cameraAPI: boolean;
        webgl2API: boolean;
        xrAPI: boolean;
        immersiveAR: boolean | null;
    };
    camera: Record<string, string | number | boolean>;
    state: string;
    targets: Record<string, {
        found: number;
        lost: number;
        ended: number;
        firstFoundMs: number | null;
        recoveriesMs: number[];
    }>;
    poses: {
        count: number;
        backends: Record<string, number>;
        scales: Record<string, number>;
        projectionSources: Record<string, number>;
        relocalized: number;
        keyframeCorrected: number;
        firstPoseMs: number | null;
    };
    quality: {
        samples: Record<string, number>;
        issues: Record<string, number>;
        diagnosis: 'heuristic';
    };
    metrics: {
        processingMs: DiagnosticStats;
        readbackMs: DiagnosticStats;
        consumerMs: DiagnosticStats;
        renderLoopMs: DiagnosticStats;
        poseStepTranslation: DiagnosticStats;
        poseStepRotationDegrees: DiagnosticStats;
        reprojectionErrorPx: DiagnosticStats;
        latestCamera: CameraMetrics | null;
    };
    odometry: {
        frames: number;
        stages: Record<typeof ODOMETRY_STAGES[number], DiagnosticStats>;
    };
    tracking: {
        frames: number;
        stages: Record<typeof TRACKING_STAGES[number], DiagnosticStats>;
        paths: Record<typeof TRACKING_COUNTS[number], number>;
    };
    renderer: {
        latest: DiagnosticRendererMetrics | null;
        peakDrawCalls: number;
        peakTriangles: number;
    };
    timeline: {
        atMs: number;
        event: string;
        detail: string;
    }[];
    observations: {
        atMs: number;
        testId: string;
        result: DeviceTestResult;
        notes: string;
    }[];
    limits: {
        sampleLimit: number;
        timelineLimit: number;
        observationLimit: number;
        quantiles: 'latest bounded samples';
        poseSteps: 'not physical jitter or drift';
        renderLoop: 'callback interval, not completed GPU frames';
        physicalValidation: 'operator-declared, not independently certified';
    };
}
type Source = Pick<WebAREngine, 'state' | 'cameraSettings' | 'targetIds' | 'onPose' | 'onStatus' | 'onError' | 'onMetrics' | 'onTargetFound' | 'onTargetLost' | 'onTrackingQuality'>;
export declare class ARDiagnostics {
    constructor(source: Source, options?: DiagnosticOptions);
    setContext(context: DiagnosticContext): void;
    mark(event: string, detail?: string): void;
    observe(testId: string, result: DeviceTestResult, notes?: string): void;
    recordError(error: Error): void;
    recordRenderer(input: DiagnosticRendererMetrics): void;
    recordRenderFrame(): void;
    probeCapabilities(): Promise<void>;
    stop(): void;
    snapshot(): DiagnosticReport;
    download(filename?: string): void;
}
export {};
```

## slam/ExperimentalMetricScale.d.ts

```ts
type WindowRejection = 'visualCoverage' | 'sensorCoverage' | 'sensorGap' | 'weakVisualMotion' | 'weakInertialMotion';
type Interruption = 'poseGap' | 'trackingLost' | 'relocalized' | 'keyframeCorrection' | 'mapReset';
type AxisValues = {
    x: number;
    y: number;
    z: number;
};
interface MotionSignal {
    windows: number;
    deviceAccelerationRmsMps2: AxisValues;
    worldAccelerationRmsMps2: AxisValues;
    integratedRmsMeters: AxisValues;
    meanAbsoluteIntegralMeters: AxisValues;
}
interface GuidedPhaseDiagnostics {
    visualPoses: number;
    visualDisplacementUnits: number | null;
    visualDisplacementMeters: number | null;
    visualCoverageMs: number;
    stationaryPoses: number;
    maxExcursionUnits: number | null;
    durationMs: number;
    samples: number;
    usableSamples: number;
    accelerationPeakMps2: AxisValues | null;
    accelerationRmsMps2: AxisValues | null;
    accelerationStdDevMps2: AxisValues | null;
    integratedWindows: number;
    weakWindows: number;
}
export interface MetricScaleDiagnostics {
    permission: 'idle' | 'listening' | 'denied' | 'unavailable';
    motionEvents: number;
    samples: number;
    usableSamples: number;
    medianIntervalMs: number | null;
    largestGapMs: number;
    visualFrames: number;
    medianVisualIntervalMs: number | null;
    pairedWindows: number;
    relativeResidual: number | null;
    metersPerUnit: number | null;
    windowsEvaluated: number;
    windowsAccepted: number;
    rejectedWindows: Record<WindowRejection, number>;
    interruptions: Record<Interruption, number>;
    fitState: 'waiting' | 'inconsistent' | 'accepted';
    fitAttempts: number;
    timing: {
        comparableWindows: number;
        estimatedOffsetMs: number | null;
        zeroOffsetResidual: number | null;
        bestResidual: number | null;
    };
    lastTimingFit: MetricScaleDiagnostics['timing'] | null;
    motionSignal: {
        all: MotionSignal | null;
        weak: MotionSignal | null;
        guided: MotionSignal | null;
        guidedWeak: MotionSignal | null;
    };
    guidedPhases: Record<string, GuidedPhaseDiagnostics>;
}
export declare class ExperimentalMetricScale {
    start(): Promise<boolean>;
    stop(): void;
    setGuidedMotionCapture(active: boolean): void;
    hasStableVisualTracking(now?: number): boolean;
    pauseGuidedMotionPhase(): void;
    setGuidedMotionPhase(id: string): void;
    diagnostics(): MetricScaleDiagnostics;
    guidedReturnError(outboundId: string, inboundId: string): number | null;
    resetMap(): void;
    interrupt(reason?: Interruption): void;
    observe(time: number, worldFromCamera: Float32Array, stationary?: boolean): number | null;
}
export {};
```

## slam/OdometryBackend.d.ts

```ts
import type { CameraIntrinsics } from '../Pose.js';
import type { ImageObservation } from '../tracking/types.js';
export interface OdometryConfig {
    intrinsics: CameraIntrinsics;
    opencvURL?: string;
    seed?: ImageObservation;
    keyframeCorrection?: boolean;
    floorROI: {
        x: number;
        y: number;
        width: number;
        height: number;
    };
}
export interface OdometryMapSnapshot {
    version: 1;
    intrinsics: CameraIntrinsics;
    scale: 'relative' | 'metric';
    mapId: string;
    keyframes: {
        descriptors: Uint8Array;
        points: Float32Array;
        view: Float32Array;
    }[];
    groundPlane?: {
        worldFromPlane: Float32Array;
        inliers: number;
    };
    currentViewCaptured?: boolean;
}
export declare const ODOMETRY_STAGES: readonly [
    "grayMs",
    "cornersMs",
    "flowMs",
    "flowNormalMs",
    "flowWideMs",
    "flowRetryMs",
    "initializationMs",
    "poseMs",
    "mapUpdateMs",
    "keyframesMs",
    "planeMs",
    "planeFitMs",
    "planeConsensusMs",
    "relocalizationMs",
    "workerMs"
];
export type OdometryTimings = Partial<Record<typeof ODOMETRY_STAGES[number], number>>;
export declare const ODOMETRY_SCAN_HINTS: readonly [
    "low-texture",
    "move-sideways",
    "map-initializing",
    "plane-unverified",
    "return-to-map",
    "map-matches-insufficient",
    "map-pose-unverified",
    "map-pose-confirming",
    "surface-ready"
];
export type OdometryScanHint = typeof ODOMETRY_SCAN_HINTS[number];
export type OdometryEstimate = ({
    status: 'initializing' | 'lost';
    mapId: string;
} | {
    status: 'tracked';
    mapId: string;
    worldFromCamera: Float32Array;
    projectionMatrix: Float32Array;
    scale: 'relative' | 'metric';
    trackedPoints: number;
    environmentReady?: boolean;
    processingMs?: number;
    reprojectionErrorPx?: number;
    relocalized?: boolean;
    keyframeCorrected?: boolean;
    stationary?: boolean;
    groundPlane?: {
        worldFromPlane: Float32Array;
        inliers: number;
    };
}) & {
    timings?: OdometryTimings;
    scanHint?: OdometryScanHint;
};
export interface OdometryBackend {
    processFrame(frame: {
        rgba: Uint8ClampedArray;
        width: number;
        height: number;
        timestampMs: number;
    }): OdometryEstimate | Promise<OdometryEstimate>;
    reset(): void | Promise<void>;
    exportMap?(includeCurrentView?: boolean): OdometryMapSnapshot;
    importMap?(snapshot: OdometryMapSnapshot): void;
    checkVisualReference?(action: 'capture' | 'verify', id: string, timestampMs: number): VisualReferenceResult;
}
export type VisualReferenceResult = {
    status: 'captured';
    points: number;
} | {
    status: 'verified';
    inliers: number;
    reprojectionErrorPx: number;
    medianImageShiftPx: number;
    directReturnUnits: number;
    trajectoryDeltaUnits: number;
} | {
    status: 'unavailable' | 'insufficient-support' | 'missing-reference';
};
export interface OdometryModule {
    createOdometryBackend(config: OdometryConfig): Promise<OdometryBackend>;
}
```

## tracking/events.d.ts

```ts
import type { ARPose } from '../Pose.js';
import type { OdometryScanHint } from '../slam/OdometryBackend.js';
export type TrackingIssue = 'low-texture' | 'small-target' | 'blur' | 'high-motion' | 'insufficient-matches' | 'occlusion-or-out-of-view' | 'device-load';
export interface FrameQuality {
    gradient: number;
    laplacianVariance: number;
    motionPixels: number;
    targetSizePx: number;
    featureCount: number;
    inliers: number;
    reprojectionErrorPx: number;
}
export interface TrackingQualityEvent extends FrameQuality {
    targetId: string;
    timestampMs: number;
    state: 'tracking' | 'recovering' | 'lost';
    score: number;
    processingMs: number;
    issues: TrackingIssue[];
    diagnosis: 'heuristic';
}
export interface TargetFoundEvent {
    targetId: string;
    timestampMs: number;
    pose: ARPose;
}
export interface TargetLostEvent {
    targetId: string;
    timestampMs: number;
    retained: boolean;
    reason: 'lost' | 'removed' | 'stopped';
}
export interface TargetVisibilityEvent {
    targetId: string;
    visible: boolean;
    reason: 'tracked' | 'recovering' | 'lost' | 'removed' | 'stopped' | 'policy';
}
export interface AREventMap {
    scanGuidance: {
        hint: OdometryScanHint;
        timestampMs: number;
    };
    targetFound: TargetFoundEvent;
    targetLost: TargetLostEvent;
    trackingQuality: TrackingQualityEvent;
    targetVisibility: TargetVisibilityEvent;
}
```

## tracking/types.d.ts

```ts
import type { CameraIntrinsics } from '../Pose.js';
import type { ImageTrackingProfile } from './profile.js';
import type { FrameQuality } from './events.js';
export interface ImageObservation {
    rgba: ArrayBuffer;
    width: number;
    height: number;
    timestampMs: number;
    sessionId: number;
    intrinsics: CameraIntrinsics;
    projectionSource?: 'calibrated' | 'estimated';
    cameraFromMarker: Float32Array;
    imagePoints: Float32Array;
    objectPoints: Float32Array;
    markerCorners: Float32Array;
}
export type TrackingResult = {
    sessionId: number;
    timestampMs: number;
    processingMs: number;
    quality?: FrameQuality;
    targetId?: string;
    profile?: ImageTrackingProfile;
} & ({
    status: 'not-found';
    matrix: null;
} | {
    status: 'tracked';
    matrix: Float32Array;
    projectionMatrix: Float32Array;
    projectionSource: 'calibrated' | 'estimated';
    inliers: number;
    reprojectionErrorPx: number;
    reference: ImageObservation;
});
export interface TrackingFrameRequest {
    type: 'FRAME' | 'FRAME_BATCH';
    id: number;
    buffer: ArrayBuffer;
    width: number;
    height: number;
    sessionId: number;
    timestampMs: number;
    intrinsics: CameraIntrinsics;
    projectionSource: 'calibrated' | 'estimated';
}
export interface TrackingBatchResult {
    results: TrackingResult[];
    processingMs: number;
    profile?: ImageTrackingProfile;
}
```

## wrappers/aframe-component.d.ts

```ts
import type { Object3D, Camera } from 'three';
import type { WebAREngine } from '../WebAREngine.js';
import { ThreeCameraBackground } from './ThreeCameraBackground.js';
interface ComponentInstance {
    data: {
        target: string;
        physicalWidth: number;
        targetId: string;
    };
    el: HTMLElement & {
        object3D: Object3D;
        sceneEl?: {
            camera?: Camera;
            object3D?: Object3D;
        };
    };
    unsubscribe?: () => void;
    originalAutoUpdate?: boolean;
    originalVisible?: boolean;
    removed?: boolean;
    camera?: Camera;
    cameraAutoUpdate?: boolean;
    background?: ThreeCameraBackground;
    releaseBackground?: () => void;
    releaseCamera?: () => void;
}
interface AFrameRegistry {
    registerComponent(name: string, definition: {
        schema: {
            target: {
                type: 'string';
                default: string;
            };
            physicalWidth: {
                type: 'number';
                default: number;
            };
            targetId: {
                type: 'string';
                default: string;
            };
        };
        init(this: ComponentInstance): void;
        update(this: ComponentInstance, previous: {
            target?: string;
            physicalWidth?: number;
            targetId?: string;
        }): void;
        remove(this: ComponentInstance): void;
    }): unknown;
}
export declare function registerAFrameComponent(AFRAME: AFrameRegistry, engine: WebAREngine): void;
export {};
```

```ts
import { ThreeARScene } from './ThreeARScene.js';

export interface ARSceneElement extends HTMLElement {
    readonly app: ThreeARScene | null;
    readonly engine: WebAREngine | null;
    readonly updateComplete: Promise<void>;
    readonly diagnostics: ARDiagnostics | null;
    readonly placementState: PlacementState;
    confirmPlacement(): void;
    getDiagnosticsReport(): DiagnosticReport | null;
    downloadDiagnostics(): void;
    start(): Promise<void>;
    stop(): Promise<void>;
    refresh(): Promise<void>;
    enableSLAM(options?: SurfaceTransitionOptions): Promise<SurfaceTransitionResult>;
}
export interface ARModelElement extends HTMLElement {
    readonly model: ThreeARModel | null;
    readonly updateComplete: Promise<void>;
    reload(): Promise<void>;
    playAnimation(nameOrIndex: string | number, options?: ARAnimationOptions): void;
    pauseAnimations(): void;
    resumeAnimations(): void;
    stopAnimations(): void;
}
export interface ARVideoElement extends HTMLElement {
    readonly video: ThreeARVideo | null;
    readonly updateComplete: Promise<void>;
    reload(): Promise<void>;
    play(): Promise<void>;
    pause(): void;
}
export declare function registerARComponents(options?: ARComponentsOptions): void;
```

---
Source: docs/en/advanced.md

# Advanced API and extensions

Choose the level of integration that matches the application.

| Need | Entry point |
| --- | --- |
| Camera stream and frames only | `CameraManager` |
| Image processing and target matching | `Tracker` |
| Precompile an image target | `ImageCompiler` |
| Native immersive AR and hit testing | `SLAMManager` |
| Optical odometry and local relocalization | `OpticalFlowSLAM` |
| Coordinate camera, targets and backend switching | `WebAREngine` |

When driving `Tracker` directly, respect frame ownership for transferred pixel buffers and the worker's backpressure. Stop frame production and dispose of workers when the application ends. Preserve camera intrinsics when adjusting the frame dimensions. For custom pose consumption, start with [coordinate conventions](concepts.md), then read the signatures in the [generated API](api-generated.md).

---
Source: docs/en/architecture.md

# Implemented architecture

| Layer | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| Camera | Permission, video track, frame scheduling and capture settings. |
| Workers and WASM | Feature extraction, matching and optical processing away from the UI thread. |
| Image tracker | Marker compilation, frame-to-frame tracking, geometric checks and redetection. |
| Spatial tracking | Native XR hit testing or optical motion and surface estimates. |
| Engine | Lifecycle, target events, pose delivery and backend coordination. |
| Wrappers | Three.js and A-Frame scene updates, models, video and declarative elements. |

Workers report transforms and diagnostics to the engine. Rendering may continue between tracking updates, which allows animations to remain smooth while pose processing runs at a different cadence. The public API can be integrated without the declarative layer. See [advanced API](advanced.md) and [implementation checks](verification.md).

---
Source: docs/en/contributing.md

# Development, tests and contributions

Install the Node.js version specified by the repository and restore the locked dependencies with `npm ci`. Run the checks relevant to the change from the repository root.

```sh
npm run check
npm test
npm run build
npm run docs:check
npm run test:browser
```

For tracking changes, report the device, browser, backend, performance preset and test scene. Compare acquisition, steady tracking and recovery independently. For public API changes, update the examples, both manuals, and the declaration-derived reference in the same change. See [implementation verification](verification.md) and [physical-device acceptance](device-validation.md).

---
Source: docs/en/verification.md

# Implementation verification

Use separate checks for the behavior and environment each layer needs.

| Check | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run check` and `npm test` | Type contracts and unit regressions. |
| `npm run build` and `npm run check:package` | Compiled entry points, declarations and distribution artifacts. |
| `npm run docs:check` and `npm run docs:test-browser` | Documentation references, rendered navigation and browser smoke checks. |
| `npm run test:browser` | Browser integration and repeatable automation scenarios. |
| Physical-device run | Real camera permissions, focus, video decoding, gestures, heat and spatial behavior. |

Browser automation and prerecorded inputs make regressions repeatable. Collect live results separately for native XR and optical tracking. See [the device checklist](device-validation.md).

---
Source: docs/en/device-validation.md

# Acceptance on physical devices

Run the same scenarios on desktop, iPhone and Android where supported. Keep camera/browser versions, tested backend and assets with each result. For weaker devices, repeat a run with `performance="battery"` and compare both the render experience and detection reliability.

- **Camera.** Grant and deny permission, stop, restart, and return from a background tab.
- **Images.** Acquire both a large and a small marker, tilt it, obscure it and bring it back.
- **Interaction.** Select a model, drag and pinch while keeping the page controls usable.
- **Content.** Play an animated GLB and a video, then swap content during the session.
- **Spatial.** Place on a textured surface, walk around it, lose tracking and try to recover.
- **Maps.** Save a local optical map, restart and revisit the same viewpoint.
- **Capture.** Try saving a photo and a recording when the device and browser offer capture.

Record unavailable native features separately from failed tests. The optical backend and WebXR may produce different scale and recovery results. See [diagnostics](diagnostics.md) for collecting reproducible evidence.

---
Source: docs/en/ai-guide.md

# Integration contract for AI assistants

Start with [the first HTML application](getting-started.md) and the [declarative reference](declarative.md). Use the [generated TypeScript reference](api-generated.md) and [machine-readable API](../api.json) for exact names and signatures.

1. Prefer the hosted standalone script and custom elements for plain HTML.
2. Use image URLs directly. Precompiled targets are optional for normal JPG/PNG setup.
3. Keep target IDs identical across registration, pose events and rendering.
4. Ask the user for the real image width if physical size matters.
5. Use a user action to start the camera. Serve on localhost for desktop development and trusted HTTPS on phones.
6. Name the spatial backend and explain its scale when showing placement.
7. For dynamic apps, preserve the current session when changing content and release it when the page unmounts.
8. Check API spelling and attribute defaults against the reference. Use tested examples for advanced integrations.

See [recipes](recipes.md) for complete patterns and [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) for failure messages.

---
Source: docs/en/glossary.md

# Glossary

| Term | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| Anchor | Stored transform used to keep virtual content at a placement. |
| Chroma key | Technique that removes a selected background color from video. |
| Descriptor | Compact representation of a local image feature for matching. |
| Drift | Accumulated spatial pose error over time. |
| GLB | Binary glTF container for 3D assets. |
| Hit test | Query for a surface intersection from a ray in an XR session. |
| Keyframe | Selected frame whose features and pose help describe a local map. |
| Optical flow | Estimated movement of image points between frames. |
| Parallax | Relative image motion caused by changing viewpoint. |
| Pose | Position and orientation in a reference coordinate system. |
| Redetection | Searching for a known image again when tracking needs recovery. |
| Relocalization | Recovering a camera pose relative to a previously observed map. |
| SLAM | Simultaneous localization and mapping. |
| WASM | WebAssembly, used for computational workloads in the vision workers. |
| WebXR | Browser API for immersive XR sessions on supported devices. |
